title: Extracting the transverse coefficient as a tangential formal power series
statement: Let $L$ be a field, let $m,r\geq0$, and use the formal power series rings of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For $f\in L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m,Z_1,\ldots,Z_r]]$ and $\delta\in\mathbf N^r$, define its transverse coefficient $\operatorname{implicitTransverseCoeff}_{\delta}(f)\in L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m]]$ by $[W^{\alpha}]\operatorname{implicitTransverseCoeff}_{\delta}(f)=[W^{\alpha}Z^{\delta}]f$ for every $\alpha\in\mathbf N^m$. Thus it is the coefficient series of $Z^{\delta}$ when $f$ is expanded in the transverse variables, with no convergence or finite-support condition on $f$.

source.document: Bierstone--Milman, Canonical desingularization in characteristic zero by blowing up the maximum strata of a local invariant, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), 207--302
